overview: White brings the queen out at once to eye f7, preparing Bc4 for a quick Scholar's-mate-style attack. Black simply develops with 2...Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6, when White's queen is exposed to ...Nd4 or ...d5 and loses time. The idea is a cheap trap for beginners; against correct play White is worse because the queen blocks the knight on g1 and gets harassed.

white_ideas.idea: Qf3 and Bc4 hitting f7 for a quick attack
Hope Black ignores the threat and falls for a cheap mate
Retreat with c3 or Nc3 and play a normal game if the attack fails

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6, protecting f7 and gaining time on the queen
Strike with ...Nd4 or ...d5 to chase the queen
Castle and use the extra development for a long-term edge

typical_structures.structure: King's pawn open game where White's queen blocks the g1 knight

character.notes: Early queen sortie with traps; mostly one-sided: Black develops with tempo while White has few real threats. Little forcing play against a prepared opponent.

soundness.notes: Dubious for White; early queen move that loses time against correct development.

structure.notes: e4/e5 centre untouched, open game but undecided.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom or never play it; a surprise on weaker opponents.

level.notes: No theory but a dubious line is never beginner.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black harasses the queen with ...Nd4 and takes the initiative.
